chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about a man who dies and there is no one with him to wash him except women, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'His wife should wash him, or a female relative if there is one for him, and the women pour water over him by pouring, and regarding the woman, when she dies, her husband inserts his hand under her shirt, so he washes her.'
ai.seo_question: Who washes a deceased man if only women are present, and how does a husband wash his wife?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the gender dynamics of ghusl al-mayyit, prioritizing spousal intimacy for modesty preservation. It establishes that a husband washes his wife by inserting his hand under her garment, while a wife or female relative washes a man with water poured over him, reflecting the juristic principle of minimizing exposure between non-mahram genders.
